title: Reduction Determinism Conditions

basis.scope: Canonical reduction determinism conditions for REDUCE_025 outputs after local confluence is defined, including reduction priority semantics, deterministic choice, and bounded outcome stability without asserting universal determinism.

core_rule.statement: Determinism is bounded by canonical evaluation order and reduction priority; Choose(C) selects a unique lawful reduction among admissible candidates; repeated evaluation yields equivalent outcomes within the admissible subclass; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define the bounded conditions under which REDUCE_025 is deterministic. This patch specifies deterministic execution for admissible continuation subclasses without asserting universal determinism.

canonical_claims.statement: Determinism is bounded by canonical evaluation order and reduction priority.
Choose(C) selects a unique lawful reduction among admissible candidates.
Bounded determinism does not imply termination.
Bounded determinism does not imply global confluence.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Determinism
formal_objects.definition: A property indicating that a continuation expression has a unique lawful reduction outcome under the canonical evaluation order and reduction priority.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Priority
formal_objects.definition: The canonical ordering used when multiple lawful reductions are simultaneously admissible.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Choice Function
formal_objects.definition: The deterministic selection function that chooses the next lawful reduction according to canonical reduction priority.

formal_objects.name: Deterministic Continuation Class
formal_objects.definition: The class of continuation expressions satisfying the bounded determinism conditions.

requirements: Identical reduction outcome for repeated evaluation

canonical_conditions.description: All typed transition rules are satisfied.
EVAL_024 produces the same admissibility state for repeated evaluations.
Priority(R) selects the same lawful reduction whenever identical reduction candidates exist.
Choose(C) is deterministic for identical continuation states.
Repeated execution produces equivalent NF(C), pNF(C), or classified ⊥C_x outcomes.

determinism_classes.condition: Canonical priority or choice function not established.
Multiple lawful reductions remain unresolved under current calculus.

choice_function_rules: Choose(C) operates only on lawful reduction candidates.
Reduction priority is evaluated after EVAL_024.
Reduction traces remain diagnostic and do not influence selection.
Equivalent traces remain independent of deterministic selection.
invariants: Determinism is evaluated only after successful evaluation.
Determinism does not imply global confluence.
